subject: Observability onboarding readiness & next steps
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: sophie@platformops.io
Date: 2026-11-20T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Observability onboarding readiness & kickoff prep

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get PlatformOps on our dedicated stack. Before we lock the kickoff, could you confirm a few readiness items so Marissa and our SREs can tailor the first two weeks of work?

Quick list:
- Expected peak tokens/sec and typical sequence length distributions
- Primary environments (prod/staging) and network access constraints (VPC peering, IP allowlist)
- Preferred tracing backend (Jaeger/Lightstep/Datadog) and whether you can run our tracing hook collector in staging
- Any existing alert taxonomy (pager escalation, on-call rotation) and whom we should loop in for routing
- Procurement: do you have an existing MSA or do we kick-off DocuSign for our standard SOW?

If you can share a point of contact for procurement and SREs, we’ll attach a tailored onboarding checklist and sample runbook for review.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm readiness answers (by Tue 11/24)
2) 60-min kickoff with engineering + SREs (we can host Wed 11/25 or Thu 11/26)
3) Delivery of initial dashboards + tracing hooks in staging within 10 business days after kickoff

Attaching a short checklist we use internally.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: observability-onboarding-checklist.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
From: sophie@platformops.io
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rajiv@platformops.io
Date: 2026-11-23T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding readiness & kickoff prep

Hi Jonas,

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side:

- Peak: ~1.2k tokens/sec during ETL windows, typical median ~120 tokens/sec. Sequence lengths average ~256 tokens.
- Environments: We have staging (shared VPC) and prod (isolated VPC). Staging can do outbound to your collector over TLS; production needs IP allowlist + TLS.
- Tracing: We use Lightstep for traces; happy to host your tracing hook in staging.
- Alert taxonomy: We have Sev1/Sev2/Sev3 definitions — procurement will want a one-page summary for escalation. Our SRE lead is Rajiv (cc’d).
- Procurement: I’m looping in procurement@platformops.io — they prefer to review the MSA in parallel to technical onboarding.

Availability: Wed 11/25 11:00–12:30 PST works best for a 60-min kickoff.

Also: Could you share your sample runbook and a short checklist for alert routing? We want to align internal responders with your suggested routing patterns (eg. which alerts land as PagerDuty critical vs Slack ops-channel).

Best,
Sophie Nguyen
Head of Platform | PlatformOps
sophie@platformops.io
+1 (510) 555-1432
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: sophie@platformops.io
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-24T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding readiness & kickoff prep

Sophie — perfect, thanks for the details and for looping Rajiv/procurement. I’ve scheduled the kickoff for Wed 2026-11-25 11:00 PST and invited the following Redwood folks: Marissa (CS Lead), Evelyn (SRE lead), and Dev (Implementation Engineer).

Attached:
- observability-onboarding-checklist.pdf (updated)
- sample-runbook-template.md (markdown stub we use to document alert flow, runbook steps, and postmortem links)

Notable implementation notes for the kickoff:
- Tracing hook: Evelyn will cover the Lightstep collector integration and a small sidecar we recommend for enriched span tags (tenant_id, request_path, model_version).
- Dashboards: Marissa will demo the recommended starter dashboards (latency heatmap, token throughput, cache hit ratio, KV cache sizes).
- Alert routing: we’ll propose an initial set of alerts mapped to your Sev1/2/3 taxonomy and a canary schedule for tuning thresholds.

Action items for PlatformOps before kickoff:
- Confirm IP allowlist range for prod (Rajiv)
- Share a short doc with current PagerDuty escalation policies (Procurement can redact billing details)
- Grant staging access to our collector IP: 34.82.10.99 (temporary)

See you Wednesday — we’ll bring a proposed two-week implementation plan covering tracing hooks -> dashboards -> runbook handoff -> SLOs + alert tuning.

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Internal: PlatformOps onboarding plan (prep + owners)

Team — prepping for Wednesday’s kickoff. Draft timeline and owners below; I’ll present the timeline during the call and capture any changes.

Week 0 (kickoff + environment access)
- Jonas: kickoff and account intro, capture PlatformOps requirements
- Dev: verify staging collector connectivity, set up tracer sidecar repo (repo: rw/onboarding/platformops-trace)
- Evelyn: pre-check list for prod allowlist and TLS cert expectations

Week 1 (traces + dashboards in staging)
- Dev + Evelyn: deploy tracing hook in staging, validate span enrichment (tenant_id, model_version)
- Marissa: provision starter dashboards and share link to dashboard folder (Drive)

Week 2 (alert routing + runbook handoff)
- Marissa + Dev: map PlatformOps Sev1/2/3 -> PagerDuty/Slack routing; propose a 48-hour tuning window
- Marissa: finalize runbook template and postmortem section; handoff to PlatformOps SREs

Deliverables before pilot:
- Starter dashboards link
- Sample runbook (attached)
- Alert taxonomy mapping doc (we’ll deliver after first tuning window)

I’ve attached the sample-runbook-template.md and added comments to the checklist. Specific asks for the kickoff:
- Rajiv to confirm IP allowlist by EOD Mon 11/30
- Sophie to provide PagerDuty escalation doc or a redacted summary

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior CS Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Observability onboarding readiness & kickoff prep

Thanks team — the kickoff went well. A few confirmations and next items from PlatformOps:

- Procurement will review the MSA this week; procurement@platformops.io will follow up on any redlines.
- Rajiv confirmed prod allowlist range: 52.23.149.0/24 — he’ll send the formal CIDR and firewall owner contacts in a separate email.
- Tracing: we confirmed Lightstep acceptance in staging; Rajiv asked for the sidecar config example for model_version tagging.
- Alerts: we prefer critical incidents to route to PagerDuty for any Sev1 with >1m downtime; otherwise, route to #platform-ops Slack.

Next asks from our side:
1) Please share the sample-runbook-template.md (we have it), and can you drop a short example in the checklist showing a real alert mapped to runbook steps?
2) DocuSign MSA link to start parallel legal review (Procurement prefers parallel).

We’ll target the first post-kickoff demo of dashboards + live trace example on Fri 12/10. If that schedule looks good, please confirm.

Best,
Sophie
